title: Exploring how compound interest grows savings for education
learningObjectives: Understand how time and compound interest can increase savings for future education goals
Explain that starting to save early helps money grow faster through compound interest
Describe how increasing principal, rate, or compounding frequency can help savings grow even faster

explanations.text: Compound interest means you earn interest on both the money you save and on interest already earned, so the balance grows over time.

evidence.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.

explanations.text: For example, a $1,000 principal earning 5 percent compounded once per year grows to $1,050 after one year and to $1,102.50 after two years.

evidence.quote: So let's say you invest $1,000 (your principal) and it earns 5 percent (interest rate) once a year (the compounding frequency).
The second year, you would have $1,102.50.

explanations.text: Savings can grow even faster by adding to principal, increasing the interest rate, increasing how often interest compounds, and by starting early.

evidence.quote: Increasing the compounding frequency or your interest rate or adding to your principal can help your savings grow even faster.
The sooner you start saving in an account that pays interest, the faster your money can grow.
